Canonical mail-server first (.1), then propagate to 6 siblings (.2-.7) per workspace canonical-template rule.

{"description":"Per-extension-server integration of draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04 (refreshed from -02 names by JMAP-5kpy). Each opted-in extension-server MemoryBackend needs three integration points, all served by the reusable baseline in jmap-metadata-server (JMAP-5kpy):

**1. query_objects filter matching (-04 §3.6):** for each leaf FilterCondition, call `MetadataCondition::take_from(&mut leaf, &info)` before decoding the type's own condition (strips the six metadata* fields; maps errors to invalidArguments / unsupportedFilter), then AND `cond.matches(obj["metadata"], viewer's privateMetadata)` with the type's own match. Metadata values live in the stored object under the `metadata` and `privateMetadata` keys.

**2. get_changes ignoreMetadataOnlyChanges and updatedProperties (-04 §3, §3.3):** `MetadataOnlyChanges::from_request(arg, using)` (no metadata capability => Ignore). Record per-update changed properties in the change log with `changed_properties(before, after)`; fold the window into `ChangedProperties::record`; drop ids where `is_metadata_only` under Ignore (excluded ids do not count toward maxChanges); `updated_properties(updated, mode, count_props)` gives the response field (Mailbox passes the RFC 8621 §2.2 count names).

**3. /set validation (-04 §2.1, §2.1.1, §3.2):** rule 1 (notFound, then forbidden without maySetMetadata) stays in the server; then `check_metadata_write(kind, entry, stored, &info)` (rules 2-3, migration case), apply the patch (invalidPatch), then `check_metadata_depth(entry, written, &info)` (rule 4). Errors map to invalidProperties with `err.property()`.

Canonical mail-server first (.1), then propagate to 6 siblings (.2-.7) per workspace canonical-template rule.

**Depends on:** JMAP-5kpy (baseline helpers).
